notToBeConfusedWith.name: Kina Lillet
notToBeConfusedWith.note: The original, more bitter quinine-forward formula this bottle replaced in 1986; the recipes that name it were written against the discontinued product, not this one.

notToBeConfusedWith.name: Cocchi Americano
notToBeConfusedWith.note: A separate producer's quinquina, often used as a closer match to the discontinued Kina Lillet's bitterness; not the same bottle as this record.

forms.label: Standard
forms.animalOriginNote: A wine-based aperitif; wine is routinely fined with isinglass or gelatine and the producer does not publish whether this bottling is animal-fined.
forms.sourceNote: Open Food Facts record submitted under the Lillet brand account states 17% alc./vol., 8.8 g sugar and 130 kcal per 100 ml, which is internally consistent: 17 ml ethanol/100 ml at 0.789 g/ml is 13.4 g alcohol (94 kcal at 7 kcal/g) plus 8.8 g sugar (35 kcal at 4 kcal/g) totals 129 kcal, matching the stated 130. Density has no measured liquid source and is taken from density-classes.json's 'fortified-wine' class (1.03 g/ml); nutritionPer100g is the per-100-ml figure divided through that density. Lillet Blanc is the modern, lower-quinine reformulation sold since 1986; the original Corpse Reviver No. 2 recipe predates it and named the discontinued Kina Lillet.
